problems: The blind guess ('vague stylised figure with a rounded head, possibly a bird or seated humanoid') only partly matches. It catches 'bird' but not a gull with spread wings in flight, and the figure does not read clearly as either.
The figure is small, roughly 60x150 px in a 530x555 frame, and sits in the upper-middle with most of the canvas empty.
Labels collide: 'head, the eye of the gull' overlaps 'beak tip', and 'breast, the warm centre of the body' overlaps 'left wing bend, where the wi...'. The wing-bend label is unreadable.
The left wing bend (97938) sits almost on top of the breast star (97649), so the wing does not read as a separate joint from the body. There is no visible shoulder-to-wing break.

The wings are lopsided: the left wingtip (98036) hangs low at about (195,242), while the right wingtip (96229) is higher at about (339,215). Wings should be symmetric about the body axis for a gull in flight.
The blue secondary lines form a tangle of crossing curves through the body and wings. They look like a second, unclear outline rather than a clean silhouette, and they cut across the gold lines.
The figure is upright, with the head at top and the tail at bottom, which is correct.
output.advice:
Verdict is redraw. The figure needs to read as a gull in flight.

1. Scale and centre: enlarge the whole figure about 2x around its centre (~260,195) so it fills roughly 60% of the frame height. Keep the body axis vertical.
2. Head and beak: keep the head star 97675 (~224,131) as the rounded head top. Place the beak tip 97278 (~256,127) so the beak points horizontally forward from the head, and move the 'head, the eye of the gull' label above the head so it does not collide with the beak label.
3. Body: keep the breast star 97649 (~226,176) as the warm centre of the body, at the middle of the torso. Draw a short, rounded body outline from the head down to the tail.
4. Wings: move the left wing bend 97938 out to the left shoulder, about 30-40 px left of the breast, so the wing visibly joins the body at a shoulder. Extend the left wingtip 98036 and right wingtip 96229 to mirrored positions about the body axis (for example, left ~(120,190) and right ~(330,190)), so the wings are level and symmetric. Draw each wing as a single curved stroke from shoulder to wingtip.
5. Tail: keep the tail tip 96665 (~303,268) below the breast on the body axis, or move it to ~(226,290) so the tail sits directly under the body rather than off to one side.
6. Silhouette: fill the body and wing outline from the gold lines, and drop the blue secondary curves or reduce them to one clean outline so they do not tangle with the gold lines.
7. Labels: stagger the label positions (head above, beak to the right, wing bend to the left, breast below) so none overlap."
